newsitem.title: USA: Calif. reaches deal to back Golden Eagle Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Calif. reaches deal to back Golden Eagle Insurance.

text.p: California's insurance commissioner said Monday he has signed an agreement with Liberty Mutual Group to back Golden Eagle Insurance Co policies.

Under the terms of the reinsurance agreement, Boston-based Liberty Mutual will assume 100 percent of all losses on virtually all new and renewal policies issued by Golden Eagle from March 1 until the completion of Golden Eagle's rehabilitation plan, Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said.

"This historic agreement means that Golden Eagle policyholders can rest easier knowing their claims will be backed by Liberty Mutual, a company with over $5 billion in surplus," Quackenbush said in a statement.
Quackenbush also announced that he issued a request for proposals for the rehabilitation plan for Golden Eagle.

"Due to the increasing number of parties expressing an interest in this transaction, it is necessary to establish a standardized process by which companies can develop and submit their proposals," Quackenbush said.

Last month, Quackenbush served a court order to take over control and operation of San Diego-based Golden Eagle Insurance Co, one of the largest writers of workers' compensation insurance in the state.
At the time, Quackenbush said certain business practices by the management of the privately held company had put both the company and consumers at risk.
